claims.text: A machine-learning-accelerated ab initio method can substantially reduce the cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties for high-entropy systems.
The proposed method can maintain accuracy while reducing computational cost.
The method is intended to evaluate both solid and fluid states of high-entropy systems.
The intervention is to implement machine-learning acceleration in ab initio free-energy evaluation.
Machine-learning algorithms will be integrated into ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
Machine-learning predictions will accelerate free-energy calculations by reducing the need for explicit molecular-dynamics simulations.
The method will produce a significant computational-cost reduction relative to explicit ab initio free-energy evaluation and TOR-TILD.
The method will maintain the accuracy of fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties relative to explicit ab initio workflows and TOR-TILD.
The proposed composition domain is high-entropy systems.
The proposed temperature domain is the high-temperature regime relevant to fusion.
Cost reduction and accuracy may vary with implementation and the complexity of the high-entropy system.
The method can be benchmarked by comparing phase free energies, phase-transition temperatures, and entropy values against explicit ab initio molecular dynamics and TOR-TILD.
Failure to reproduce benchmark phase free energies and derived observables within 5% would falsify the hypothesis.
